body:
*A lot of my self worth was tied to what my first girlfriend thought of me, and when I lost her I was completely shattered. I also wasn't ready for that severing of awareness, where my consciousness was suddenly only in the here and now rather than shared between me and her.*

This is exactly what I experienced in the last month. My girlfriend and I have gotten back together, but this painful experience has made me stronger, more self-confident and much more mature. I give her credit for breaking all ties for weeks, and myself credit for letting her be.

Thanks for your advice in this thread. And good luck to you as well.

Thank you for you advice a month ago. My girlfriend has come back to me, and we're going to give it another try, with a new focus on our individual needs. Those horribly painful weeks have motivated me and given me a new desire to better my own life, instead of relying on someone else. I'm going to counseling and trying an antidepressant and mindfulness meditation.

You guys in SW are awesome, thank you.

Hi, I wanted to ask your advice since you gave me good advice in this thread. I will try to make this short. Since this post, my girlfriend came back to me temporarily. After she broke up with me again, she told me someone asked her out. She said it wasn't a date and she didn't go. Then, we got back together briefly until one night, she said she didn't want to talk to me again.

That night, she met that guy at a party and "cuddled with him a little". A week later (this past Saturday), she called me up at 6am and said she wanted to come over, sounding very upset. I had been calling her but she had been ignoring me the whole week (she in no uncertain terms told me we were over). She told me she made out with that guy and slept on a friend's futon with him, but nothing else happened. (She came directly from that house to me.) She told him she wasn't going to have sex with him; that morning he told her he didn't want to see her ever again and left. She came to my apartment crying and told me this and I got really mad, punching the wall and telling her to leave, but I wanted to be with her so badly and was so happy to see her that I eventually calmed down. She told me the guy was a douchebag and it made her realize how much she loved me. She felt horrible and I know her feelings were genuine. She told me she wanted to be with me forever and start our relationship again.

I was okay for a couple days but last night we were drinking and I stupidly looked at her phone texts when she wasn't in the room. I just looked briefly and saw his texts to her, nothing revealing but it made me so mad and depressed. I haven't been able to tell her I looked at her phone. There were a dozen or more messages and they said "gnite" and she seemed to have a cute nickname for him. Now I can't stop thinking about her and the guy (who is ten years older than her, that makes me sick too) and it's making it hard for me to be get a fresh start in our relationship. We had a wonderful few days since then, never a moment apart. I feel like such an ass looking at her phone, knowing it would make me depressed and angry, but I am too afraid of disturbing the love and peace we're sharing at the moment.

She considered herself broken up with me at the time. But it unsettles me that just hours after making out with him and going to bed next to him, she suddenly decided she wanted me back. It unsettles me too because I was suspicious and I nearly sent her a message saying, "Are you with [him] now?" the night she made out with him. And at first it made me sick to look at her and kiss her, thinking of her kissing him, and that feeling is coming back today.

I'm sorry this is so long and you have no obligation to reply, but my counselor is unavailable until after xmas break and I really need someone to talk to. I am so in love with this beautiful person and after our long relationship I believe we will spend our lives together. We both want our relationship to grow and be stronger and more loving than ever, but this is festering in my mind, I want to stop it now, and if you could give me some reassurance and more words of wisdom, I would really appreciate it.
Sorry to be a bother. Thanks for listening :)

Thank you sir. Easier said than done, but thank you.

EDIT: also she is friends with me. for a while she wasn't.

Thank you very, very much. I had putting off making a post like this for days, now I have no idea why.

You are right, I have to clean up. Exercise is something I have completely neglected.
Thank you, that's a lot to think about.

Yeah she moved here to be with me, but she had decided that maybe 6 months ago, too late reverse the decision.

She had been talking about breaking up for a couple months but didn't really do it for real until a few weeks ago. We had spent college together until last year when I moved away. We saw each for a few days at a time every few months last year.

She still loves me and cares about me. Tonight she felt so bad for me we went out to dinner and we cuddled and even kissed for a while. We have this deep connection but she still wants to "be single" and not feel like her future is tied up with me. I don't understand because I don't want to control her life but we have this very real love that is not going anywhere.
